**Clinical Note Template**

**1. Patient Information**

Name: Arthur Miller
Age/Gender: 65 years/Male
Hospital Stay Dates: October 26, 2023 to November 15, 2023 (with multiple admissions/discharges)
Admitting Diagnosis:  Suspected colorectal cancer with anemia
Discharge Diagnosis: Stage II Colon Cancer, Anemia, Post-operative ileus (resolved)


**2. Visit Details**

**[October 26, 2023, 14:30]**

Provider Role: Emergency Physician
Reason for Visit:  Progressive fatigue, weight loss (15 lbs in 2 months), dark stools.
Interventions:  Complete blood count (CBC), comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP), fecal occult blood test (FOBT), abdominal examination.
Findings/Results:  CBC revealed hemoglobin 9.2 g/dL (low), hematocrit 27.6%.  CMP unremarkable except for slightly elevated liver enzymes. FOBT positive for occult blood. Abdominal exam revealed mild tenderness in the lower left quadrant.
Treatment Plan:  Admitted to the hospital for further investigation.  IV fluids initiated.  Consult with gastroenterology requested.

**[October 27, 2023, 09:00]**

Provider Role: Gastroenterologist
Reason for Visit:  Evaluation of anemia and positive FOBT.
Interventions:  Colonoscopy with biopsy.
Findings/Results:  Colonoscopy revealed a 4cm mass in the sigmoid colon.  Biopsies taken.
Treatment Plan:  Patient to remain hospitalized pending biopsy results.  Iron supplementation initiated.

**[October 28, 2023, 11:00]**

Provider Role: Gastroenterologist
Reason for Visit:  Review of biopsy results.
Findings/Results:  Biopsy confirmed moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the colon.
Treatment Plan:  Surgical consult requested for resection.  Discussion with patient and family regarding treatment options.

**[October 30, 2023, 08:00]**

Provider Role: Surgeon
Reason for Visit:  Pre-operative evaluation for sigmoid colectomy.
Interventions:  Chest X-ray, ECG, blood typing and cross-matching.
Findings/Results:  All pre-operative tests within normal limits.
Treatment Plan:  Sigmoid colectomy scheduled for October 31, 2023.

**[October 31, 2023, 15:00]**

Provider Role: Surgeon
Reason for Visit:  Post-operative assessment following sigmoid colectomy.
Interventions:  Sigmoid colectomy performed.  Pathology report pending.
Findings/Results:  Procedure completed without complications.  Patient stable in post-anesthesia care unit (PACU).
Treatment Plan:  Close monitoring of vital signs, pain management, bowel rest, IV fluids.

**[November 2, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role: Surgeon
Reason for Visit:  Post-operative day 2.
Interventions:  Assessment of bowel sounds, abdominal examination.
Findings/Results:  Absent bowel sounds.  Mild abdominal distension.
Treatment Plan:  Continued bowel rest, nasogastric tube placement for decompression.

**[November 5, 2023, 14:00]**

Provider Role: Surgeon
Reason for Visit:  Post-operative ileus.
Interventions:  Abdominal X-ray.
Findings/Results:  Abdominal X-ray showing dilated loops of bowel consistent with ileus.
Treatment Plan:  Continued bowel rest, intravenous fluids, and close monitoring.  Discharge planned once bowel function returns.

**[November 8, 2023, 09:00]**

Provider Role: Surgeon
Reason for Visit:  Progress evaluation.
Interventions:  Assessment of bowel sounds, abdominal examination.
Findings/Results:  Bowel sounds returning.  Abdominal distension resolving.
Treatment Plan:  Advance diet as tolerated.  Removal of nasogastric tube.

**[November 10, 2023, 11:00]**

Provider Role:  Oncologist
Reason for Visit:  Discussion of adjuvant chemotherapy.
Interventions:  Discussion of treatment options.
Findings/Results:  Pathology report confirmed Stage II colon cancer with clear margins.
Treatment Plan:  Adjuvant chemotherapy recommended.  Referral to medical oncology.


**[November 15, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role: Surgeon
Reason for Visit:  Discharge planning.
Interventions:  Physical examination.
Findings/Results:  Patient stable, bowel function restored.  Wound healing well.
Treatment Plan:  Discharged home.


**3. Key Events During Hospitalization**

* Sigmoid colectomy performed on October 31, 2023, by Dr. Ramirez. Procedure successful.
* Post-operative ileus developed on November 2, 2023, requiring nasogastric tube placement. Resolved by November 8, 2023.
* Diagnosis of Stage II colon cancer confirmed on October 28, 2023.


**4. Ongoing Management and Care**

* IV fluids and pain medication administered throughout the hospitalization.
* Nasogastric tube placed and removed as needed for bowel decompression.
* Iron supplementation initiated to address anemia.
* Nutritional support provided.
* Close monitoring of vital signs and bowel function.
* Consultations with gastroenterology, surgery, and oncology.


**5. Discharge Summary**

Discharge Medications:  Iron sulfate 325mg PO BID,  Acetaminophen 500mg PO PRN for pain,  Senna 8.6mg PO PRN for constipation.
Follow-up Instructions:  Follow-up appointment with surgeon in 2 weeks.  Referral to medical oncology for adjuvant chemotherapy.  Return to the emergency department if fever, increasing abdominal pain, or worsening of symptoms.
Prognosis:  Good prognosis with appropriate treatment.  Adjuvant chemotherapy will improve the chances of long-term disease-free survival.

Findings/Results:  Surgical wound is clean, dry, and well-approximated.  Minimal tenderness to palpation in the lower abdomen.  Patient reports regular bowel movements without significant discomfort.  Pain well-controlled with Acetaminophen.  Reports good appetite and energy levels improved compared to pre-operative state.
Treatment Plan: Continue current medication regimen.  Schedule follow-up appointment in 4 weeks.  Encourage regular physical activity as tolerated.  Advice on dietary fiber intake to prevent constipation.


**[December 12, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role: Medical Oncologist (Dr. Chen)
Reason for Visit:  Initiation of adjuvant chemotherapy.
Interventions:  Review of pathology report, discussion of treatment plan, physical examination, complete blood count (CBC), comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP).
Findings/Results:  CBC and CMP within normal limits.  Patient well-informed about the risks and benefits of chemotherapy.  Treatment plan discussed in detail, including potential side effects and management strategies.
Treatment Plan:  Adjuvant chemotherapy regimen with FOLFOX (5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin) initiated.  First cycle administered today.  Close monitoring for side effects, including nausea, vomiting, fatigue, and neuropathy.  Follow-up appointment scheduled for next week to assess for adverse effects and adjust treatment as needed.  Patient provided with educational materials on chemotherapy side effects and management.


**[December 19, 2023, 15:30]**

Provider Role: Medical Oncologist (Dr. Chen)
Reason for Visit:  Follow-up after first cycle of FOLFOX chemotherapy.
Interventions:  Assessment of chemotherapy side effects,  physical examination, CBC, CMP.
Findings/Results:  Patient reports mild fatigue and nausea, well-managed with antiemetic medication (Ondansetron).  CBC shows slight decrease in WBC count, within expected range for chemotherapy.  CMP unremarkable.  No signs of peripheral neuropathy.  Patient’s overall condition is good considering the treatment.  Patient reports good compliance with prescribed medications.
Treatment Plan:  Continue with FOLFOX chemotherapy regimen.  Adjust dosage of Ondansetron to manage nausea.  Close monitoring for any signs of neutropenia.  Schedule blood tests before next cycle to monitor blood counts.  Encourage increased fluid intake and a healthy diet.  Educate patient about the importance of reporting any unusual symptoms immediately.
